Bluetooth Low Energy(BLE)

Bluetooth Low Energy is a protocol supported since Bluetooth 4.0. Compared with Bluetooth Classic, Bluetooth Low Energy features extremely low power consumption and faster transmission speed, but transmits a small amount of data. It is commonly used in various intelligent electronic products that have a relatively high requirement on a battery life and require only a small amount of data to be transmitted, such as an intelligent wearable device, an intelligent home appliance, and a sensor, and is widely applied to a wide range of scenarios.

1. work mode

The Bluetooth low energy protocol defines several roles, or operating modes for devices. Currently, the Bluetooth Mini Program supports the following working modes:

  • Central mode：The central device may scan a peripheral device, and after finding that a peripheral device exists, establish a connection to the peripheral device, and then may use a service (Service) provided by the peripheral device.
  • peripheral mode: not supported currently
  • Beacon: not supported currently。

In general, the mobile phone will play the role of a central device, using data provided by peripheral devices for processing or display. The Mini Program provides a low-power Bluetooth interface that defaults to setting the phone as the central device.

Precautions

In the Mini Program, the current Mini Program Bluetooth BLE only supports the mobile Bluetooth device in host mode. On a terminal device, you only need to call ma.openBluetoothAdapter to initialize the Bluetooth adapter once to use the Bluetooth capability of the Mini Program.

2. Communication Protocol

After two Bluetooth low energy devices establish a connection, data exchange between the two parties is based on the GATT (Generic Attribute Profile) specification. A profile (Profile) may be defined according to the specification, to describe a service (Service) provided by the Bluetooth device.

There are several key concepts in the whole communication process:

  • Profile: A profile is a collection of services predefined by the Bluetooth standard and does not exist on a Bluetooth device. For Bluetooth devices to be compatible with each other, they only need to support the same profile. A Bluetooth device can support multiple profiles.
  • Service: A Bluetooth device can provide multiple services, such as the battery level information service and system information service. Each service is uniquely identified by a UUID.
  • Characteristic: Each service contains zero or more characteristics. For example, the power information service has a characteristic to indicate the power data. A characteristic consists of a ** value and zero or more descriptors**.. When the Bluetooth device is communicated, the communication is mainly completed by reading and writing the value of the characteristic. Each characteristic is uniquely identified by a UUID.
  • Descriptor: A descriptor is a defined property that describes the value of a feature. For example, a Descriptor may specify a human-readable description, a range of values for a feature value, or a unit of measure specific to a feature value. Each descriptor is uniquely identified by a UUID.

As shown in the following figure, each Bluetooth device may provide multiple services, and each service may have multiple characteristics. You can read and write the value of the corresponding characteristic based on the protocol of the Bluetooth device to communicate with the Bluetooth device.

3. UUID (Universally Unique Identifier)

According to the Bluetooth 4.2 protocol specification (Vol 3, Part B, section 2.5.1 UUID), a UUID is a 128-bit unique identifier used to identify a Service, a Characteristic, and etc.

To reduce the burden of storing and transmitting 128-bit UUID values, the Bluetooth consortium pre-allocates UUIDs that have a common part called the 00000000-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB. Therefore, the pre-allocation of UUID of can also be represented using 16 bits or 32 bits, with 16-bit UUIDs being the most common. Using 16-bit and 32-bit UUIDs reduces the storage and transmission load. The UUID defined by the developer cannot conflict with the pre-allocated UUID.

In the Mini Program, the parameters for ma.startBluetoothDevicesDiscovery and ma.getConnectedBluetoothDevices support 16/32/128-bit UUIDs. In the parameters of other interfaces,

  • iOS supports 16-bit and 128-bit UUIDs directly.
  • Android 8.0.9 and later versions support 16-bit, 32-bit, and 128-bit UUIDs.
  • Versions earlier than Android 8.0.9 support only 128-bit UUIDs. Developers need to manually add 128-bit UUIDs. Place filling method is as follows:

    128-bit UUID = 16-bit UUID * 2^96 + Bluetooth Base UUID 128-bit UUID = 32-bit UUID * 2^96 + Bluetooth Base UUID

    for example

    0x180F -> 0000180F-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB The return values of all interfaces are 128-bit UUIDs.

4. Process of Using Central Devices

4.1 Initialize the Bluetooth module.

Before using the Bluetooth APIs, you must call ma.openBluetoothAdapter to initialize the Bluetooth adapter module. Other APIs can be called only after the initialization is successful. If Bluetooth is disabled or your phone does not support Bluetooth, an error message will be displayed. In this case, the Mini Program Bluetooth module has been initialized, and the API related to Bluetooth BLE can be called to start Bluetooth interaction. Developers should consider compatibility with the situation that users turn on/off the Bluetooth switch during the use of the Mini Program, and provide necessary prompts to improve usability.

ma.openBluetoothAdapter({
  success: () => {
    // Initialized successs
  }
})

4.2 Scan and discover Bluetooth peripherals

After the Bluetooth module is initialized successfully, you need to scan peripheral devices by running ma.startBluetoothDevicesDiscovery. When a Bluetooth peripheral device is scanned, the ma.onBluetoothDeviceFound event is called back and the scanned device is returned. Scanning devices consumes system resources. Call ma.stopBluetoothDevicesDiscovery to stop scanning after the required device is found. If you do not manually stop the search, the Mini Program API will search for 5 minutes by default. After 5 minutes, the search stops.

If a device has been connected and the device ID has been obtained, skip the scanning step.

// Listening to the event of detecting a new device
ma.onBluetoothDeviceFound((res) => {
  res.devices.forEach((device) => {
    // You can do some filtering here.
    console.log('Device Found', device)
  })
  // Stop scanning as soon as you find the device you're searching for
  ma.stopBluetoothDevicesDiscovery()
})

// Initialize the Bluetooth module
ma.openBluetoothAdapter({
  success: (res) => {
    // Start searching for nearby Bluetooth peripherals
    ma.startBluetoothDevicesDiscovery({
      success: (res) => {
        console.log('startBluetoothDevicesDiscovery successs' + res)
      }
    })
  },
  fail: (res) => {
    console.log('openBluetoothAdapter fail' + res)
  }
})

4.3 Connected device

For Bluetooth Low Energy devices to communicate with each other, a connection must first be established.

ma.createBLEConnection({
  deviceId, // deviceId of the found device.
  success: () => {
    // Connection succeeded. Obtain the service.
    ma.getBLEDeviceServices({
      deviceId,
    })
  }
})

4.4 Get Services for Bluetooth Peripherals

ma.getBLEDeviceServices({
  deviceId, // deviceId of the found device.
  success: (res) => {
    for (let i = 0; i < res.services.length; i++) {
      if (res.services[i].isPrimary) {
        // Select a main service for communication based on service requirements.
      }
    }
  }
})

4.5 Write the feature value of the service.

ma.getBLEDeviceCharacteristics({
  deviceId, // deviceId of the found device.
  serviceId, // One of the services id found in the previous step
  success: (res) => {
    for (let i = 0; i < res.characteristics.length; i++) {
      let item = res.characteristics[i]
      if (item.properties.write) { // The characteristic value can be written
        // This example is to send a 0x00 hexadecimal data to the Bluetooth device.
        // In practice, data should be sent according to the specific device protocol.
        let buffer = new ArrayBuffer(1)
        let dataView = new DataView(buffer)
        dataView.setUint8(0, 0)
        ma.writeBLECharacteristicValue({
          deviceId,
          serviceId,
          characteristicId: item.uuid,
          value: buffer,
        })
      }
    }
  }
})

4.6 Disconnecting and Turning Off the Bluetooth Adapter

When you are finished, disconnect and turn off the Bluetooth adapter at the appropriate time.

5. Precautions

  • For the read, write, and notify operations on feature values on iOS devices, the system needs to obtain feature value instances. Therefore, the input serviceId and characteristicId must be obtained from ma.getBLEDeviceServices and ma.getBLEDeviceCharacteristics.It can be used only after it is taken. It is recommended that ma.getBLEDeviceServices and ma.getBLEDeviceCharacteristics be executed before data exchange with the Bluetooth device after the connection is established.
  • The Bluetooth function can be used for indirect location. For Android 6.0 and later versions, if you do not have the location permission or the location switch is turned off, you cannot search for devices.
  • On Android, when some models obtain device services, the 00001800 and 00001801 UUID services are displayed. This is a system behavior. Do not use these two services.
  • The functions of establishing and closing a connection must be invoked in pairs. If the connection is not closed in time to release resources, exceptions may occur.
  • When transferring data to and from a Bluetooth device, you need to be aware of the MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit). If the data size exceeds the MTU, an error occurs. It is recommended that the data be transmitted in segments based on the Bluetooth device protocol. If the MTU is unknown, it is recommended that the transmission unit be 20 bytes.
